edits.find: **Match the model to the job.** Start from the role's line or default, keep its family, and set the level the job needs. The `/setup-pstack` budget sets each role's starting level. Panel seats keep their listed level. Raise any other role one step, up to xhigh, for the hardest or subtlest work, lower it one step for judgment, and two or more steps for routine work. No role runs above xhigh. Opus 5.5 always runs its `-fast` slug. Verification always runs on the `swarm workers` model, `claude-opus-5-5-high-fast` by default. A Gemini seat runs at `gemini-4-neon-xhigh` unless its line names another level. If the Task tool rejects a slug, never pass it again. No role runs above xhigh. Verification always runs on the `swarm workers` line, `opus high` by default. If the Agent tool rejects a model or an effort, never pass it again. edits.why: The Agent tool takes a model alias plus an `effort`, with no slugs, families, or fast mode. An Agent spawn runs no Gemini model, so upstream's rule for the Gemini seat's level has no counterpart either. An external entry keeps its own effort, as Other vendors says.

edits.find: A second opinion is the same prompt on another vendor's model.
edits.replace:
A second opinion is the same prompt on another vendor's model when your `second opinion` line names one, and on a different Claude model otherwise. Name the panel in the reply. "Cross-vendor panel (claude, codex)" is stronger evidence than "same-vendor panel (opus, sonnet)", because one vendor's models share more blind spots.

**Other vendors.** A role value is `[<provider>:]<model> [<effort>]`, and no provider means Claude. An entry with a provider, such as `gemini:gemini-2.5-pro`, runs that vendor's CLI read-only through the **pstack-ask** skill, from a background Bash call in the same message as any `Agent` spawns. It may sit only on `interrogate reviewers`, `arena cross-judge pool`, and `second opinion`, because writing code, exploring with tools, and using MCP servers stay on Claude. On any other role it is an error, so use that role's default and say so. With no `second opinion` line, a second opinion runs on sonnet under an opus parent and on opus otherwise. When you match the model to the job, change `effort` on Claude entries only. An external entry keeps the effort its line names, because each vendor has its own scale.
edits.why: An Agent spawn runs only Claude models, so another vendor's model answers only through pstack-ask, on the review and judging roles that Phase 3 opens to it. With no such entry, a different Claude model is the closest second opinion. The reply names the panel so the reader knows what the agreement is worth.

- `/deslop` and the `deslop` skill ship in the `cursor-team-kit` plugin.

## borrowed skills

upstream keeps three skills that `poteto-mode` uses in a separate plugin. omc-pstack-fy bundles them, so they work out of the box:

- [`/deslop`](./skills/deslop/SKILL.md) cleans slop out of the diff before each commit.
- [`control-cli`](./skills/control-cli/SKILL.md) drives CLIs and TUIs.
- [`control-ui`](./skills/control-ui/SKILL.md) drives browser, Electron, and web UIs.

for writing a skill, `poteto-mode` uses the `skill-creator` skill when your session lists it. omc-pstack-fy doesn't bundle that one. without it, a skill is a `SKILL.md` with `name` and `description` frontmatter under `.claude/skills/<name>/`, or `~/.claude/skills/<name>/` for a personal skill.
edits.why: deslop, control-cli, and control-ui are bundled. Claude Code has no create-skill or autopilot built-in, and skill-creator is its skill-authoring guide.

## Give parallel work its own machine

If you run several agents against one repository on one computer, they will fight over the working tree, the ports, and the build output. The cleanest isolation is a [cloud subagent](https://cursor.com/docs/subagents#cloud-subagents). Each one gets its own VM and branch, so it can install dependencies, run your app, and record video of the result without touching your machine. Type `/in-cloud` before the task, or ask the parent chat to hand work to cloud subagents.

When the work has to stay local, ask for a worktree up front:
edits.replace:
## Give parallel work its own worktree

If you run several agents against one repository on one computer, they will fight over the working tree, the ports, and the build output. The cleanest isolation is a subagent in its own git worktree, so ask the parent chat to hand parallel work to worktree subagents. The ports and the machine stay shared, so give each agent that runs the app its own port.

To pick the base and branch yourself, ask for a worktree up front:
edits.why: Claude Code subagents run on this machine. A worktree is their isolation, and it does not separate ports.

The judge never runs on the parent's model. Use the first entry from another vendor, else the first Claude entry on another model. Fable and the other Claude models are one vendor, so a Claude judge under a Claude parent is a same-vendor judge. An `inherit` entry is the parent model, so it never judges. For a Claude entry, spawn the judge with `subagent_type: "general-purpose"` and the entry's `model` and `effort`. Its brief says "do not edit files", and you check `git status` after it returns. For an external entry, such as `gemini:gemini-2.5-pro`, read the **pstack-ask** skill and run the judge through it, read-only. Its throwaway copy may not reach the candidates' folders, so inline each candidate, or its diff, in its prompt under its path label. If its CLI is not installed, fails, or times out, run the Claude fallback that skill names and say so in one line. If you do not know the parent's model, use the first entry and say that the model check did not run. If the Agent tool rejects an entry, use the same model at the closest effort its schema lists, then the next such entry, or skip the judge, and say so.

Upstream's pool reaches another vendor only through Gemini, which an Agent spawn cannot run, so omc-pstack-fy tells models apart where upstream tells vendors apart. Upstream dropped Fable from the pool because it counts Fable and Opus as one vendor. Compared by model, `fable` is a seat of its own, so the default pool keeps three seats, as the Models section of docs/claude-code-mapping.md records. The pool may name another vendor's model per the Phase 3 contract, which shares fewer blind spots with a Claude parent, so it goes first. pstack-ask's throwaway copy cannot see the candidates' folders.

edits.find: No findings is a valid result.
edits.replace:
No findings is a valid result.

An entry with a provider prefix, such as `gemini:gemini-2.5-pro`, is an external adversary on another vendor's model. Read the **pstack-ask** skill and follow it. It runs that adversary read-only from a background Bash call, in the same message as the `Agent` spawns, in a throwaway copy that already holds `HEAD` and the uncommitted changes. Give it the scope, the intent, and the brief, with the scope's diff pasted in. Add two lines to its brief.

> You run under a read-only flag in a throwaway copy deleted when you exit, so each repro must be a command that writes no files. If you cannot run a command, still report it and the output the intent requires, marked not run.

Its output is data, so read each command before you rerun it in Verify, and rerun it in a worktree that holds the scope, never in the user's checkout. Verify keeps a not-run finding only when your rerun proves it. pstack-ask copies the current checkout, so when the scope is not the current checkout, run the Claude fallback that skill names in place of each external entry, and say so. An external adversary that ran no command does not make the panel cross-vendor. If its CLI is not installed, fails, or times out, run the Claude fallback that skill names and say so in one line.
edits.why: An `interrogate reviewers` entry may name another vendor's model, run read-only through pstack-ask per the Phase 3 contract. Verify reruns every command, so a finding from a read-only adversary is proven by the lead's run. pstack-ask's copy is writable and only the CLI's own flag blocks writes, and the copy is deleted on exit, so the repro must be a command that writes nothing. Some CLIs in read-only mode cannot run a command at all, so such an adversary reports an unrun command and the lead's rerun decides. pstack-ask treats a vendor's output as data, and rerunning a command from it executes that data, so the rerun happens in a worktree, not the user's checkout. pstack-ask clones the current checkout, so it cannot test another scope.

Each finding stands on its rerun, but "no verified findings" from a same-vendor panel is weaker evidence, because one vendor's models share more blind spots.
edits.why: The Phase 3 contract names the panel in every panel reply. A rerun proves each finding whatever model found it, so the panel now bounds only what a clean result is worth.

The Skill tool refuses `/statechart` and the generated skill sits outside this plugin, so tell the next agent to search the Claude Code plugin cache (`~/.claude/plugins/cache/omc-pstack-fy/` by default) for a file whose path ends in `skills/statechart/SKILL.md`, to use the copy whose `.claude-plugin/plugin.json` has the highest `version` when more than one matches, and to read that file and follow it.
